A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KnapSpec work. All main-text and appendix material is readable, and the algorithms, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding experiments across six benchmarks in Table 2, alongside throughput, pruning, layer-selection and optimization-interval analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds stochastic-decoding comparisons in Table 3 and hardware-profiling and speedup results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The latency-aware knapsack search, dynamic programming, TPT selection and confidence-based drafting exit remain unchanged, including the appendix algorithms. v2 expands calibration documentation and evaluation settings without documenting a changed KnapSpec procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIME24, AIME25 and MMLU-Pro reasoning, plus GovReport, PG19 and BookSum summarization. The added sampling and hardware experiments remain within this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AR, DEL, SWIFT and CLaSp, and the new sampling comparison uses the same comparator set. Table 1's ADMG-to-ASD correction identifies the same cited method; newly cited long-context methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 supplements greedy decoding with nucleus sampling at temperature 0.7, top-k 50 and top-p 0.95 using Qwen3-8B and Llama3.1-8B. Appendix C adds GovReport testing across three GPU types. The existing main-comparison settings are retained.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a check of robustness to stochastic decoding, while Appendix C tests hardware portability on RTX 6000 Pro, RTX A6000 and RTX 4090. Existing pruning, optimization-interval, layer-distribution and throughput-proxy analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly specifies least-squares linear regression for estimating latency coefficients. This adds statistical estimation documentation, not evidence of increased repetitions. The existing 20-run SWIFT optimization description is unchanged, and no confidence intervals, seed lists or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 2's results and the existing plotted findings are unchanged. New Table 3 reports KnapSpec speedups of 1.07-1.23× under sampling; Table 4 reports fitted latency coefficients, feasible-case speedups of 1.24-1.28×, and an out-of-memory result for Llama3.1-8B on RTX 4090. These are additional conditions, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Lemma 4.1, its assumptions and Appendix A proof are unchanged, as are the TPT equations, DP recurrence and complexity analysis. Appendix C explicitly parameterizes the previously described constant MLP and linear attention latencies without introducing a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free, hardware-aware knapsack selection, cosine-similarity justification and superior SSD speedups up to 1.47×. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the sampling results as evidence of robustness across deterministic and stochastic decoding. Appendix C additionally argues that hardware-specific calibration explains consistent acceleration across GPU settings and connects attention costs to KV-cache access and memory bandwidth.

D1.justification: v2 adds an official implementation link and specifies offline least-squares calibration of constant MLP and affine attention latency models. Table 4 supplies GPU/model identities and fitted coefficients. These clarify previously generic profiling instructions; the underlying calibration procedure is not established to have changed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds TriForce, MagicDec and SpecExtend to contextualize long-context speculative decoding through KV-cache and attention optimization. Holtzman et al. is added for nucleus sampling. SWIFT and DEL publication updates concern existing references rather than new research relationships.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section structure are retained. Changes include focused explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgments and front-matter updates, correction of ASD terminology, reversal of the two Appendix B subsections, and moving Algorithm Description from Appendix C to D.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 4 and clarifies Table 2's headings and caption by spelling out speedup and identifying acceptance rate as alpha. Existing figures are retained; appendix Figures 5 and 6 exchange numbering and placement, and the algorithm listings are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's greedy-only evaluation and generic profiling description, v2 provides useful sampling and hardware robustness evidence, explicit latency-fitting details and code-access information. These strengthen validation and reproducibility while retaining the original results and theory. The improvement is bounded by the limited additional sampling and hardware configurations.
